purpose: Reduce timestep sensitivity of log ray-map Jacobians without changing geometry or the telegrapher PDE.
motivation: Completed KO6 N2049 dt/2-to-spatial logJ difference ratio .224876 exceeds the 10 percent target; field and constraint ratios are much smaller. Piecewise-linear speed interpolation has a discontinuous derivative at each grid node.
candidate: Optional monotonic C1 piecewise-cubic Hermite speed interpolation (PCHIP), using the derivative of that same interpolant for logJ. Keep linear interpolation as a control. No ray value may feed back into geometry, flux, elliptic shift or timestep guards.
implementation_checks: Independent value/derivative oracle, affine-field exactness, monotonicity and continuity across nodes on mapped grids.
Actual nonzero-flux RK-stage rays against an independent implementation.
Geometry and auxiliary flux bitwise unchanged between ray interpolation choices.
Exact checkpoint preservation of positions, logJ and compensated state.
Default linear path preserves existing results.
nonlinear_checks: Short dt/dt2/dt4 pilot compares interpolation choices at identical physical parameters.
Any selected mode still needs complete t10 three-grid ray/geometry convergence and independent timestep controls.
A finite smooth interpolant cannot prove absence of continuum characteristic crossing.
status: Implemented and tested; completed t3 pilot reduces active-ray logJ timestep differences by about100 but fails all-ray time/space ratio .253519 due terminal exit integration. Dense exit repair is separately declared; no candidate admitted.

pilot.interpretation: Pilot tests diagnostic timestep sensitivity only. Coarse physical runs need not pass main acceptance; no thresholds relaxed.
